name: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (adult)

meta.title: Adult ALL in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (adult), B- and T-lineage
meta.population: Adults >=18; newly diagnosed (Ph-negative, Ph-positive, T-ALL) and relapsed/refractory settings. Pediatric ALL is its own catalog row per the granularity rule.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for adult ALL showing how an in silico engine routes a phased, response-adapted pathway: lineage and Ph gates select the protocol, MRD checkpoints re-route mid-treatment (immunotherapy, transplant), and relapsed/refractory options are ranked with honest evidence grades. Curative intent changes the math and the conversation: the shared display is X-in-100 in durable remission, not median months. Scope boundaries: complication management renders as co-interventions only; dosing is out of scope; response-rate endpoints (CR/MRD) display but never rank against…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic patient. Training only. Not medical advice.
meta.response: CR/CRi + measurable residual disease (MRD) by flow or NGS, threshold 1e-4

stages.label: Presentation
stages.question: How urgent, and what must be stabilized first?
stages.decision: Stabilize (tumor lysis, hyperleukocytosis, infection) and complete the diagnostic workup.

stages.label: Diagnosis & risk
stages.question: What lineage, what drivers, what risk?
stages.decision: Assign lineage, Ph status, Ph-like signature, and genetic risk group.

stages.label: Frontline protocol
stages.question: Which protocol - and what does the next 2-3 years look like?
stages.decision: Select the phased protocol (induction -> consolidation -> maintenance) by age, fitness, lineage, Ph status.

stages.label: MRD checkpoints
stages.question: Is the disease molecularly gone - and what does the answer change?
stages.decision: Response-adapted re-routing at end of induction and consolidation.

stages.label: Transplant decision
stages.question: Does allogeneic transplant add more than it costs?
stages.decision: AlloHSCT in CR1 vs continue protocol +/- immunotherapy.

stages.label: Relapsed / refractory
stages.question: It's back - which rescue, in which order?
stages.decision: Blinatumomab, inotuzumab, CAR-T (brexu-cel / obe-cel), nelarabine (T-ALL), trial, or palliation.

stages.label: Trial matching
stages.question: Which studies fit - and why?
stages.decision: Rank open studies; name the unlock.

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: Age routes the protocol family (pediatric-inspired through 39 per CALGB 10403) and carries cited hazard modifiers; it is never a hard gate by itself.
Patient.helpPatient: Age helps pick which protocol family fits - younger adults do best on pediatric-style regimens.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Intensive protocols require ECOG <=2; CAR-T trials enrolled ECOG <=1. Modifiers fire at 2 and >=3. (v1.1's '3-4' bucket is now the 3-4 slider range.)
Patient.helpPatient: How much normal activity is possible right now.

Patient.label: Comorbidity burden
Patient.help: High burden applies a cited hazard modifier and closes the transplant arm.
Patient.helpPatient: Other health problems that make intensive treatment harder.

Presentation.label: Presenting WBC
Presentation.help: Hyperleukocytosis is a triage flag and an adverse-risk modifier.
Presentation.helpPatient: A very high white-cell count means treatment starts urgently.

Presentation.label: CNS status
Presentation.help: Scales CNS prophylaxis intensity (a co-intervention, never ranked); CNS3 carries a modifier.
Presentation.helpPatient: Whether leukemia cells are in the spinal fluid - it changes the preventive treatment, not the goal.

Diagnostic gates.label: Lineage
Diagnostic gates.help: CD19/CD22 immunotherapies are B-lineage; nelarabine is T-lineage. Always resulted with flow.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: Which family of white cells the leukemia came from - it selects the drug family too.

Diagnostic gates.label: BCR::ABL1 (Ph)
Diagnostic gates.help: The master routing gate: Ph-positive OPENS the TKI-based, increasingly chemo-light pathway (unlike GBM's IDH gate, which excludes). Pending blocks frontline ranking.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: One gene test that picks between two completely different treatment roads - worth waiting a few days for.

Diagnostic gates.label: Ph-like signature
Diagnostic gates.help: Trial-relevant kinase signature; also an adverse-outcome flag in CALGB 10403.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: A gene pattern that can point toward specific studies.

Antigens.label: CD19 expression
Antigens.help: Gates blinatumomab and CD19 CAR-T in every setting; antigen escape is a real mechanism and a teaching point.
Antigens.helpPatient: A surface marker the strongest immune drugs need to find the leukemia.

Antigens.label: CD22 expression
Antigens.help: Gates inotuzumab; 'not tested' renders the arm as needs-data rather than blocked.
Antigens.helpPatient: The marker a second antibody drug uses.

Risk.label: Risk genetics (KMT2A / TP53 / hypodiploidy)
Risk.help: High-risk lesions set the relapse-risk prior and open the CR1 transplant conditional.
Risk.helpPatient: Certain chromosome changes make a transplant discussion more likely.

Risk.label: Donor availability
Risk.help: Transplant eligibility input; typing early is cheap insurance even when transplant is unlikely.
Risk.helpPatient: Whether a matched marrow donor exists - family typing starts early just in case.

On treatment.label: MRD at end of induction
On treatment.help: The single most consequential branch in the disease: positive routes to blinatumomab (BLAST) + transplant evaluation; negative still earned blinatumomab consolidation in E1910.
On treatment.helpPatient: The deep test a month in that tells us whether the leukemia is molecularly gone.

On treatment.label: MRD at end of consolidation
On treatment.help: Persistent MRD here is the strongest transplant indication; it opens the alloHSCT arm.
On treatment.helpPatient: The same deep test later on - it drives the transplant question.

On treatment.label: Prior blinatumomab exposure
On treatment.help: Frontline blinatumomab exposure (now standard post-E1910) changes the relapsed menu.
On treatment.helpPatient: Whether this immune drug was already used earlier.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Where you are.label: Your state (optional)
Where you are.help: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.
Where you are.helpPatient: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.

Newly diagnosed.name: Pediatric-inspired protocol (AYA)
Newly diagnosed.patient: The children's-style protocol adults up to 39 do best on - intense at first, then years of lighter maintenance.

Newly diagnosed.name: Intensive chemo + blinatumomab consolidation
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: cytopenias; blinatumomab neuropsychiatric events (higher incidence vs chemo alone in E1910)
Newly diagnosed.patient: Standard intensive chemotherapy with an immune drug woven into consolidation - the combination that moved survival in a randomized trial.

Newly diagnosed.name: Lower-intensity induction + immunotherapy (older/unfit)
Newly diagnosed.patient: A gentler backbone that leans on the antibody drugs instead of maximum chemotherapy.

Newly diagnosed.name: Ponatinib + reduced-intensity chemo (Ph+)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: arterial occlusive events (2.5% vs 1.2% imatinib in PhALLCON) - monitor
Newly diagnosed.patient: A targeted pill matched to the Philadelphia chromosome, with much lighter chemotherapy.

Newly diagnosed.name: Dasatinib + blinatumomab, chemo-free (Ph+)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN option; phase 3 confirmation (ALL2820) read out at ASH 2025
Newly diagnosed.patient: The chemo-free road: a targeted pill plus an immune drug - and the randomized trial testing it just read out in its favor.

Newly diagnosed.name: Pediatric-inspired + nelarabine consideration (T-ALL)
Newly diagnosed.patient: The T-cell version of the intensive protocol, with a T-cell-specific drug available if needed.

Newly diagnosed.name: Allogeneic stem-cell transplant (CR1)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: treatment-related mortality ~10-20% and GVHD - disclosed verbatim per honesty constraint
Newly diagnosed.patient: Replacing the marrow with a donor's - held for the situations where leftover disease or high-risk genetics make it worth the real risks.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always a valid choice; rarely chosen given curative intent
Newly diagnosed.patient: Full attention on comfort, chosen with open eyes: this disease moves fast without treatment, and the curable road exists.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Blinatumomab
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The immune drug that beat chemotherapy head-to-head at relapse.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Inotuzumab ozogamicin
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: hepatic VOD 11% (vs 1% chemo), cytopenias - flagged pre-transplant
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: An antibody that delivers chemotherapy directly into the leukemia cells - very high remission rates.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Brexucabtagene autoleucel (CAR-T)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: grade >=3 CRS 24%, neuro events 25% - REMS program
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Your own T-cells, re-engineered to hunt the leukemia - a one-time infusion with real upfront risks.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Obecabtagene autoleucel (CAR-T)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS/ICANS with comparatively low high-grade rates
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The newer CAR-T, dosed gently over two days - similar power, gentler side-effect profile so far.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Nelarabine (T-ALL)
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The T-cell-specific drug, used when the T-cell disease comes back.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Comfort first, with transfusions and symptom care that still help.

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date; every 'confirm' left in this spec is listed in the manifest staleness list.
Transplant cards must disclose treatment-related mortality alongside benefit - never benefit alone.
Comfort care remains a modeled arm, with the honest note that curative intent makes its numbers starker here than in solid-tumor trainers.
MRD branch logic is shown BEFORE results exist; pending results withhold decisions, not information.
Surrogate-endpoint approvals (PhALLCON MRD-neg CR) are labeled as surrogate; OS maturity is tracked in the manifest.
Response-rate endpoints (CR/CRi, MRD-neg CR) display with their label and never rank against survival endpoints - non-comparable metrics are labeled, not blended.
If the trainer disagrees with the paper, trust the paper.
gates: Ph/BCR::ABL1 must be resulted before frontline ranking
lineage assigns the protocol family and antigen-directed options
checkpoint decisions are withheld while MRD is pending
CD19-negative disease closes blinatumomab/CD19 CAR-T; CD22 status gates inotuzumab

surveillance.cadence: CBC and clinical review per protocol through the 2-3 year maintenance horizon; marrow + MRD on count abnormalities
